key_insight: Lead-free Co1.2Ti0.2Fe1.6O4–BaTiO3 composites achieve stronger magnetoelectric coupling when composition and sintering temperature are jointly tuned, with the best response at 30CTFO–70BTO sintered at 1200 °C.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies a practical route to optimize bulk multiferroic materials for low-power sensors, memory, spintronic devices, and actuators without using lead.
method: Solid-state synthesis of (x)Co1.2Ti0.2Fe1.6O4–(100−x)BaTiO3 composites with x = 10, 20, 30
X-ray diffraction and Rietveld refinement to confirm tetragonal BaTiO3 plus cubic spinel CTFO phases
Microstructure, dielectric/ferroelectric, magnetic, and magnetoelectric measurements across sintering conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports the highest magnetoelectric coefficient of about 1.28 mV/cm·Oe for 30CTFO–70BTO sintered at 1200 °C, showing clear dependence on composition and processing.
watch_item: The P–E behavior is lossy due to leakage from the conductive phase, which may limit ferroelectric performance and device reliability.
paper_title: Optimization of magneto-electric properties in Lead-free (x)Co1.2Ti0.2Fe1.6O4 - (100-x)BaTiO3 based composites
